who: Cassandra Lee Burke (witness; Support Coordinator, Access Disability Services; former FFG support coordinator) - statement taken by NDIS Fraud Investigator Bruce Graydon
what: Statement of Cassandra Lee Burke 'in the matter of R v Vida REID' dated 16 Feb 2023 (T62.1, 10 pages, pp1309-1318), taken about 4pm at Perth by NDIA fraud investigator Bruce Graydon (NDIA investigators Graydon and Narelle Richardson visited Access's Jull Street office that day). Burke (30) worked at FFG from June/July 2022 (receptionist, then support coordinator after 3 weeks; ~18 participants) and joined Access Disability Services (owner Paul Ugwunali) in Oct 2022. Attributes to Vida: 30 Sep 2022 staff meeting announcing work-from-home trial ('Simon and I have been talking... this is Simon's idea'); 4 Oct 2022 meeting addressing 'fraud claims' as malicious allegations/defamation; laptops collected and later returned; instructing staff to email their local MP after her arrest, drafts altered by Vida; on 25 Oct 2022 Vida introduced Burke to Ugwunali and told her she could no longer be offered work (Burke signed with Access, then was locked out of CareView by Blake Sadler: 'Vida has to sort some clients out'). On 15 Nov 2022 participant Jonathon Shapiera (living at Vida's Safety Bay house 'Malibu House') told her 'Blake' would take over as his coordinator, 'running a company for Vida and Simon called Dream Big' (first time she had heard of Dream Big); Shapiera emailed termination 1 Dec 2022 4:53pm. Pamela Cricelli (mother of participant Giuseppe Cricelli) emailed 10 Dec 2022 cancelling Burke's services as 'she was going back to Vida and Simon'. On 1 Dec 2022 outside the Jull St office, in Virginie Fanny-Dulloo's presence, Vida offered Burke a coordinator job at 'my new company' (start 9 Jan 2023, Rottnest Island Christmas trip); Burke says she knew this was Dream Big because she had 'heard' Vida and Simon Reid started the new company and had reported it to the NDIA twice (Fraud Hotline; email/phone to 'Nathan Halls' at NDIA).
notes: OCR of scanned pages. This is a witness statement (allegation), made in the criminal matter R v Vida REID and later put to Simon (T64.1 para 42(c)). It is mostly about VIDA, not Simon. Simon-specific content: only (i) Vida's remark that work-from-home was 'Simon's idea' (30 Sep 2022); (ii) Shapiera's hearsay that Blake would run 'a company for Vida and Simon called Dream Big'; (iii) Pamela Cricelli going 'back to Vida and Simon'; (iv) Burke 'heard' that Vida and Simon started the company (hearsay). The statement does NOT say Simon established or owned Dream Big or that it was an NDIS provider - cf Commission's characterisation at T64.1 para 42(c). Internal inconsistencies/oddities: para 59 (1 Dec 2022 job offer) is narrated after paras 55-58 (9-10 Dec 2022 emails); NDIA officer called 'Nathan Halls' (para 47, 72) and 'Andrew Halls' (para 19, quoted Vida remark) - name variant; Pamela's surname 'Cricelli' here vs 'Circelli' in T58 transcript; Shapiera also appears as 'Shapeira' (T44). Exhibits (texts and emails) are referred to but not reproduced.

to_whom: Tom Monks, Tom & Co Legal Pty Ltd
why: internal review of banning order; new information re Dream Big/Vitality WA
notes: Document fact. Review outcome is WORSE for Simon than the original (scope broadened) and rests in part on matters first raised on 22 Mar 2023. Penalty: $275,000/1,000 = $275 per penalty unit (consistent with FFG corporate figure $1,375,000 = 5x). Duration: 22 Dec 2027 is five years from the original 21 Dec 2022 order, not five years from the variation.

who: Sian Leathem - findings on original decision (Simon)
what: Reviewer finds original decision correct/preferable but disagrees with how the original decision-maker weighed evidence and some findings of fact. Findings she accepts: Simon is associated with Hybrid Hive (ABN 96 651 140 108, unregistered, banned permanently 21 Dec 2022) and FFG (revoked/banned 10 years 20 Dec 2022); Simon was co-director of Hybrid 17 Feb 2022-21 Aug 2022 and sole director from 22 Aug 2022; co-director of FFG 28 Aug 2020-3 Jan 2021 and again from 1 Nov 2022; SoMF (19 Oct 2022) alleges Simon and Vida are joint signatories on Hybrid's ANZ account; between 25 Jan and 10 May 2022 Assist submitted 20 claims for Hybrid services to Meghan Goodwin paid $78,491.06 to Assist then to Hybrid's ANZ account (NDIA asserts Simon received money reasonably suspected proceeds of crime); Assist lodged 11 suspicious-invoice reports re FFG and Hybrid 26 Aug-21 Sep 2022. She EXCLUDES: FFG claims for Sarah-Jane Clulow (24 Nov 2021-22 Jun 2022) because Simon was not director of FFG then; weight on the $1,485,527 expired-plan figure (minimal, per Tactical Intelligence Report); bail conditions of Vida; duplicated allegations; FFG conduct generally (considers only Hybrid from Aug-Sep 2022 reports).
notes: KEY: the reviewer applies the principle that directors answer for the entity they direct (para 38; Corporations Act s 180 care and diligence; 'I do not attribute much weight to shareholding... it is directorship that links him'). Directorship conflicts: SoMF (T45) says Vida sole director of Hybrid from 1 Dec 2021; T46 NOI says Simon director since 17 Feb 2022; this review: Simon co-director 17 Feb-21 Aug 2022 then sole; ASIC extract (T63) lists only Simon as officeholder with start 17/2/2022. Also the review accepts Simon was NOT a director of FFG during the Clulow/Aug-Sep 2022 claims - inconsistent with the 19 Oct 2022 suspension notice (T77) calling Simon a 'Director' of FFG. $78,491.06 is the same sum the FFG review (T71.1 para 40(m)(ix)) says went to Hybrid Hive and was disregarded for FFG - same money used in both.

who: Sian Leathem - findings on Simon's submissions and procedural fairness
what: Reviewer rejects Simon's procedural-fairness complaint (para 35): Simon had several opportunities (2 Dec 2022 extension, 6 Feb 2023 invitation, 22 Mar 2023 invitation) and used none; finds bail conditions irrelevant but charges against Vida relevant because the SoMF 'contain allegations that Mr Reid engaged in fraudulent activity'; attributes liability to Simon as director of Hybrid (para 38); gives NO weight to the claim of exculpatory evidence (never provided despite request) and MINIMAL weight to his 'wholesale denial' (para 40). Concludes (para 46) that 'having regard to the ongoing investigation by the NDIA and law enforcement agencies into the fraudulent conduct Mr Reid is alleged to have engaged in', Simon is 'not suitable at this time to be an NDIS provider'; period of 5 years is said to correspond with the time reasonably expected for 'current regulatory and legal processes... in relation to Mr Reid to conclude' (para 47).
notes: Commission's reasoning (contention/decision, not fact). Points of tension: (1) the ban is justified by 'allegations' and an 'ongoing investigation' - no charge against Simon is recorded; (2) the 5-year period is said to match expected time for processes to conclude, whereas the FFG internal review (T71.1 para 73) gave 3 years on the same logic (decided 7 weeks later); (3) extension of 2 Dec 2022 was granted after the submission had been lodged (para 35(a)).

who: Sian Leathem - new evidence (Dream Big / Vitality WA)
what: Reviewer treats as new evidence: ASIC Form 201 submitted by Simon 29 Oct 2022 to register Dream Big Employment Pty Ltd ('an NDIS provider'); Simon's 9 Feb 2023 1:43pm email recruiting disability support workers for Vitality WA Pty Ltd ('a company that provides labour hire workers to NDIS providers and of which Mr Reid is a director'); Cassandra Burke's 16 Feb 2023 statement 'which indicated Mr Reid had established or was the owner of a new business (Dream Big) that operated as an NDIS provider'. States Simon's involvement 'seems to have commenced around the time he was issued the banning order on 21 December 2022' and that establishing Vitality and Dream Big suggests he 'may be finding strategic or tactical ways to circumvent the terms of the banning order', justifying broader scope.
notes: CONFLICTS/GAPS: (1) the ASIC form is dated 29 Oct 2022, i.e. BEFORE the NOI (17 Nov) and ban (21 Dec 2022), not 'around the time' of the ban; (2) Burke's statement (T62.1) is hearsay/impression about 'Vida and Simon' and does not say Simon owned Dream Big or that Dream Big was an NDIS provider; (3) Fanny-Dulloo's s 56 interview (T58, 9 Mar 2023) - evidence that Simon only lodged the ASIC form as a favour - is dated 9 Mar 2023, 2 weeks BEFORE the 22 Mar 2023 notice, but the review does not list the interview among its materials; (4) the 9 Feb 2023 email was sent after the ban (21 Dec 2022) and offers staff to 'disability providers' (ban item (b) labour hire, introduced only by this variation); (5) no source is cited for Simon being a director of Vitality WA Pty Ltd (T65.1 shows email signature 'Director, Vitality Employment Services').

who: Sian Leathem, Complaints Commissioner and delegate of the NDIS Commissioner (internal review IR (10) 22/23 and ICM23/198)
what: Internal review decision (s 100 NDIS Act) on FFG's banning order: VARIED the 20 Dec 2022 s 73ZN(1)(a) banning order from 10 years to 3 years (in force from 5:30pm 20 Dec 2022 until 12:00am 21 Dec 2025 AWST), on the basis that 3 years approximates the time reasonably expected for FFG-related criminal proceedings to finish, after which it can be revisited (s 73ZO). Decision letter to Tom Monks; Attachment A varied banning order; Attachment B statement of reasons (76 paras). Review request had been received 21 Feb 2023; acknowledgment same day invited submissions by 21 Mar 2023; Monks' submission 20 Mar 2023; decision due 22 May 2023 so made outside s 100(6A) timeframe (acknowledged). Contravention of order is s 73ZN(10) civil penalty up to 1,000 penalty units, x5 for a corporation = $1,375,000. External review right: AAT within 28 days (AAT Act s 29(3)(b)(i)). Contact Pascal Moussa, Lawyer.
to_whom: Tom Monks, Tom & Co Legal Pty Ltd
why: internal review of 20 Dec 2022 ban against FFG
notes: Document fact. Leathem agrees outcome was correct/preferable but DISAGREES with original reasoning: original reused revocation reasons rather than independent reasons for a ban, and relied on a broader range of material than needed (should have been confined to fraud evidence). She decides on a narrower basis: fraud only (all other allegations 'fallen away'). Penalty-unit arithmetic: $1,375,000 / 5 = $275,000 / 1,000 = $275 per unit (not independently checked).

who: Sian Leathem (internal reviewer) - findings on original decision-maker
what: In FFG internal review reasons, Leathem concedes 'deficiencies and failings' by the original decision-maker: (a) not sufficiently providing FFG with information about some allegations (though FFG was 'on balance adequately informed' of the material); (b) not clearly communicating his view/analysis of FFG's submissions - she reviewed 'internal working documents' showing he DID consider the submissions but was not persuaded, and 'failed to clearly articulate the reason/s for giving minimal weight'. Also finds the 30 Nov 2022 submission wrongly alleged no response to extension request: Commission email of 15 Nov 2022 6:04pm from WACompliance@ndiscommission.gov.au to info@tomandcolegal.com.au attached the extension letter. Procedural-fairness matters do not form part of her decision (decision rests on fraud material put to FFG on 1 June 2023).

The 15 Nov 2022 6:04pm email send record is the Commission's evidence on the 'no response' dispute (cf T50/T54 vs T55).

who: Sian Leathem (internal reviewer) - evidence relied on
what: Evidence recited in FFG internal review reasons: (1) three complaints - 4-37380907579 (anonymous phone, 10 May 2022, Goodwin billed for services not provided while at St Barts), 4-38279458621 (PCI referral from NDIA 10 Aug 2022 recording complaint by advocate/plan nominee Elanor Smith, financial abuse of Goodwin's plan), 4-37833786005 (confidential, 20 May 2022, Clulow's support coordination funds $7,500 used, 'double dipping' across multiple companies); (2) sworn statement of Sarah-Jane Clulow 11 Oct 2022 (paras 13-18: duplicate invoices, unprovided supports, inflated charges); (3) sworn statement of Meghan Goodwin 12 Oct 2022 (paras 25-26: equivocal on fraud - Reviewer gives 'minimal weight'; only two STA stays in April 2022 and 22 Apr-2 May 2022; claims for self-managed building capacity and yard maintenance 'false'); (4) Prosecution Notice signed 18 Oct 2022 and NDIA Statement of Material Facts dated 19 Oct 2022 charging Vida Reid under Criminal Code (Cth) ss 400.9(1) (two counts) and 135.1(3) (two counts); (5) ASIC extract; briefing notes EC22-002000 and EC22-002581. She finds on the balance of probabilities FFG was 'used as a vehicle' for fraud by its key personnel, and notes 'FFG has not provided any evidence to negate' it.
notes: Allegations (complaints, sworn statements, SoFM) vs the Commission's finding (contention/decision). Complaints are described as 'closed' after NDIA liaison/suspension/legal proceedings. Reviewer holds the evidence is reliable because forensic examination of bank statements by NDIA and AFP scrutiny. Norman statement: former FFG employee Leah Norman (14 Dec 2020-Oct 2021) alleges Vida encouraged inflating coordination time and 'invoice bombing' (claiming residual plan funds).

who: Sian Leathem (summarising NDIA Statement of Material Facts dated 19 Oct 2022)
what: Reasons recite SoFM allegations: Vida and Simon Reid were joint signatories on FFG's ANZ and Westpac accounts; 'Mrs Reid and Mr Reid' allegedly caused 81 false payment requests against Goodwin and Clulow plans between 26 Nov 2021 and '22 June 2020' [sic]; NDIA investigation began 1 Sep 2022; on 30 Nov 2021 NDIA issued Goodwin a new plan, Vida requested copy and within an hour FFG lodged three claims (incl. 398 hours house cleaning 15 Oct-30 Nov 2021 = 8.46 hrs/day over 47 days) paid $43,004.60 to FFG ANZ on 1 Dec 2021; plan manager Zettai Pty Ltd t/a Assist Plan Managers submitted 14 claims 30 Dec 2021-20 Apr 2022 ($5,979.64) re Goodwin; NDIA forensic accountant: $127,475.30 of Goodwin claims for no service, of which $78,491.06 went to Hybrid Hive Pty Ltd (Leathem DISREGARDS that portion); Clulow claims by Assist $86,192.60 (24 Nov 2021-22 Apr 2022 to ANZ) and $33,816.88 (25 May-22 Jun 2022 to Westpac), forensic figure $120,009.48 no service.
notes: CONFLICT/ERROR: SoFM period given as '26 November 2021 and 22 June 2020' - year typo (should be 2022). The SoFM attributes false requests to 'Mrs Reid and Mr Reid' jointly, yet only Vida is charged (Prosecution Notice 18 Oct 2022). Reviewer says Hybrid Hive portion $78,491.06 of Goodwin sum disregarded, leaving $48,984.24 if the same arithmetic is applied ($127,475.30-$78,491.06 = $48,984.24) - this is OUR arithmetic.
